column1: # Ground truth for scripts/match_eval.py over the 18 sample images.
# Written by LOOKING AT EVERY OVERLAY, not by parsing the filenames. Inferring
# truth from stems gets this wrong in both directions and quietly reports the
# matcher as broken when it is not:
#   - Two bodies from one image are usually the same remote photographed
#     twice (GINZZU_GM-501) or the bare remote plus the same remote inside its
#   - Two images can be the same remote under different names and different
#     OCR'd codes: Sony_RM-PJ20_big reads RM-PJ20R, RM-PJ20_big_light reads
# BAD marks an extraction that is not a remote at all. These are excluded from
# recall rather than counted as failures -- they are extraction bugs already
# on the session-3 list, and scoring the matcher on them measures the wrong
# thing. Both are flagged severity 3 by scripts/audit_catalog.py.
# the body detector latched onto the HAND holding the remote: the rectified
# crop is a strip of fingernails, 2 buttons, 8.2% of the image
# extracted the red "RM-L859" packaging label strip, not either remote
# same remote as Sony_RM-PJ20_big_0, and stored UPSIDE DOWN despite
# orientation_conf 1.0 -- see the note on IndexConfig.index_both_orientations
